text: {"question":"Which observational data and analytical approach are employed to determine the present‑day matter density parameter Ωm0h2, and how does this procedure underpin the conclusion that the generalized PAge parameterizations can reduce the Hubble tension?","reference_answer":"The authors use the Planck 2018 measurement of Ωbh2 together with the fitting formulas (26) and (27) to compute Ωm0h2. They then convert this to a Hubble constant via H0 = √(Ωm0h2) × 100 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, treating the dimensionless Hubble parameter h as hEU = H0,EU/(100 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹). By combining this CMB‑derived H0 with low‑redshift data (SNIa, BAO, and the Alcock–Paczynski factor) the GPAge models are shown to fit the full dataset better than ΛCDM, thereby alleviating the Hubble tension. "}
